points.description: Introduces a useful auxiliary construction/setup that leads toward a solution (e.g. antipode of B on circle ABC, or antipode of A on circle AFP, or a coordinate/angle setup identifying key points such as the center of (AFP) and its projection onto BC).

levels.says: Constructs a relevant point but does not use it to establish a key relation.

points.description: Establishes a key geometric relation about circle (AFP) or the points X, Y with respect to BC (e.g. identifies the center/antipode of (AFP) and shows its projection onto BC, or shows the needed perpendicularity/collinearity/cyclic facts, using H reflection properties such as P on circle ABC and angle relations).

levels.says: Some correct relevant facts (e.g. P lies on (ABC), angle chasing) but no key relation toward the midpoint.
Key relation mostly established but with gaps or minor errors.

points.description: Uses the relation to show that the midpoint of XY (the projection of the center of (AFP) onto BC) is C, e.g. showing the center projects to C or CX = CY via power of a point/lengths.

levels.says: Reaches the conclusion only with an unjustified step or partial computation.

points.description: Complete, rigorous argument with correct conclusion that C is the midpoint of XY (no significant errors or unproved claims). Any valid alternative method (coordinates, trigonometry, power of a point) earns full marks.

rubric.notes: Full marks for any complete, correct proof, including alternative methods. Part marks for a useful construction (such as the antipode of B in (ABC) or of A in (AFP)) and for correct progress toward showing the center of (AFP) projects onto C. No marks for merely restating the problem or diagram-only claims.
